title: Per-symbol latency stitcher and KV-hit penalty allocator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce an attribution pipeline that stitches per-symbol (subtoken-level) timing slices across the serving stack and applies a KV cache hit 'penalty allocator' to accurately debit latency and cost to model emission positions. This will enable per-request cost breakdowns that reflect cache-induced latency variance and allow downstream dashboards and billing reconciliations to attribute delays to their real causes.
background: Current token-level telemetry aggregates at request or emission-chunk granularity which masks subtle effects caused by partial KV cache hits, prefetches and interleaved batching. Customers and finance teams need explainable per-unit cost/latency numbers for SLA reconciliation and chargebacks. Existing traces emit micro-timings at several layers but there is no deterministic way to map these timings to the originating symbol once the request passes through batching and kernel scheduling layers.
proposed_solution: 1) Add a concise per-symbol breadcrumb propagated through the runtime (symbol_id + emission_index + minimal routing tag). 2) Extend the tracing hooks to emit a 'stitch' event when a symbol exits a runtime stage (tokenize -> kv-lookup -> kernel-exec -> emit). 3) Implement a KV-hit penalty allocator that models extra latency introduced by cache misses/hits and apportions it across affected symbols proportionally. 4) Aggregate results in a lightweight ledger emitted as an event stream and consumed by the metrics pipeline for dashboards and billing reconciliation.
tasks: Design breadcrumb schema (4 bytes routing + 8 bytes id) and wire protocol changes between worker and orchestrator
Instrument runtime stages to emit stitch events with stable timestamps (monotonic clock) and breadcrumb
Implement KV-hit penalty allocator library and unit tests (C++ runtime component)
Add extraction and enrichment step in the metrics pipeline (logproc) to convert stitch events into per-symbol ledger entries
Create rollout plan with opt-in from 10% of requests, verify telemetry integrity, then ramp to 100%
Dashboard: latency waterfall per-symbol query and cache-impact heatmap
Billing reconciliation job that consumes ledger and produces per-request cost adjustments
tradeoffs: Breadcrumb traffic increases trace volume — mitigated by compact binary breadcrumb and sampling policy
Attribution heuristic for shared batching is approximate — we choose proportional allocation by compute-time contribution rather than naively splitting by token count
Additional CPU overhead in runtime for stitch events — bounded by batching of stitch emissions and async offload to the telemetry buffer
acceptance_criteria: Per-symbol ledger entries emitted for 100% of tested requests in opt-in cohort
Dashboard shows KV-hit-adjusted latency within 5% of end-to-end measured latency for sampled traces
Billing reconciliation job adjusts sample invoices and is verified by finance team
No regression in P99 latency for production traffic after 100% rollout (as measured by release staging)
dashboards: Ledger reconciliation panel: aggregated ledger vs sampled trace E2E
Anomaly panel: high discrepancy requests and top contributing symbols
rollout_plan: Week 1: feature flag opt-in for 1% of requests; smoke tests and data validation
Week 2: expand to 10%; run reconciliation against historical traces for agreement metrics
Week 3: 50% cohort with finance verification and dashboard readiness
Week 4: full rollout with monitoring and automatic rollback on alert
